summary.text: Human spaceflight is spaceflight with a crew or passengers aboard a spacecraft, often operated directly by the people on board.
It grew out of the Cold War, when Soviet cosmonaut Yuri Gagarin became the first human in space on 12 April 1961 and Alan Shepard became the first American on 5 May 1961.
People have been continuously present in space on the International Space Station since 2 November 2000, and only the US, Russia and China currently have such programs.

items.prompt: Between the first American flights and the Moon landings, NASA flew two-person Gemini missions. What were they for?

options.label: To match the Soviet three-person capsule on size
To build orbital experience and techniques for the Moon trip
To test the lander by practising on the Moon
To rescue cosmonauts stranded in orbit

items.explain: Gemini's objective was to support Apollo by developing American orbital spaceflight experience and techniques to be used during the Moon mission.

items.prompt: The Soviet Voskhod capsule achieved the first spacewalk, yet the program ended. Why?

options.label: It could never carry more than one person
Its spacewalk went wrong and was never repeated
The Soviets gave up racing the Americans
It could not maneuver in orbit the way Gemini could

items.explain: Voskhod did not have Gemini's capability to maneuver in orbit, and the program was terminated.

items.prompt: The USSR built the three-person Soyuz for its Moon programs but never landed anyone. What was missing?

options.label: A big enough rocket, since the N1 never came together
A capsule that could hold three people at once
Pilots willing to attempt the long trip
Any way at all to send a craft toward the Moon

items.explain: The USSR successfully developed Soyuz, but failed to develop the N1 rocket necessary for a human landing and discontinued its lunar programs in 1974.

items.prompt: Which statement correctly compares the first American in space with the first Soviet cosmonaut?

options.label: Shepard orbited Earth once while Gagarin flew a short suborbital hop
Shepard flew first, with Gagarin following a few weeks later
Shepard flew a suborbital flight and steered his craft by hand, unlike Gagarin
Both flights were suborbital and both men steered by hand

items.explain: Gagarin completed a single orbit, while Shepard flew a suborbital flight and, unlike Gagarin, manually controlled his spacecraft's attitude.

items.prompt: What gave the Cold War rivals rockets big enough to carry the first satellites?

options.label: Giant airplanes converted to climb into space
Missiles built to deliver nuclear weapons, adapted for orbit
Weather rockets first built for science
Cargo rockets built by private companies

items.explain: The US and the USSR developed intercontinental ballistic missiles for nuclear weapons, producing rockets large enough to be adapted to carry the first artificial satellites into low Earth orbit.

items.prompt: The original Shuttle idea had a piloted, winged first stage that flew itself back. What replaced it when plans were scaled back?

options.label: A reusable space tug
Four expendable boosters
One huge liquid-fuel stage on a parachute
Two reusable solid rocket boosters

items.explain: To reduce development risk, cost and time, the piloted fly-back booster was replaced with two reusable solid rocket boosters.
